bull_thesis: The bull case is that the only fully integrated American rare-earth producer is being marked down at exactly the moment its two structural supports go live, and that the market re-rates it back toward Wall Street's $80-ish targets over the next twelve to twenty-four months. Four things have to hold. First, the government partnership signed in July 2025 is a genuine contractual asset, not a headline: the Department of Defense (now the Department of War) guarantees a floor of $110 per kilogram on MP's neodymium-praseodymium ('NdPr' - the magnetic rare-earth pair that drives the economics) for ten years from the fourth quarter of 2025, took $400 million of convertible preferred stock and a warrant struck at $30.03 a share, lent $150 million for heavy rare-earth separation, and has committed to buy all 7,000 tonnes a year of the planned 10X magnet plant's output for ten years with a $140 million annual profit guarantee attached. That is a floor under revenue and a floor under the largest single growth project, from a counterparty that cannot default. Second, the operating ramp is real and verifiable: first-quarter 2026 revenue of $90.6 million was up 49% year over year, NdPr production of 917 tonnes up 63%, NdPr sales of 1,006 tonnes up 117%, total rare-earth oxide output of 12,983 tonnes up 6%, the first positive gross profit since 2024, and adjusted profit before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation of $36.6 million against a $2.7 million loss a year earlier. The company made its first commercial magnets in December 2025, picked the Northlake, Texas site for 10X in February 2026 and broke ground in the first quarter. Third, the commodity has already turned: the NdPr benchmark bottomed near $90 per kilogram on 1 June 2026 and recovered to roughly $133 by 1 July, so MP is now earning market prices above its own guaranteed floor - it keeps 70% of the excess. Fourth, there is a hard statutory demand cliff on 1 January 2027, when the defence acquisition rules implementing Section 844 of the 2021 defence authorisation act bar any US defence contractor from using neodymium-iron-boron or samarium-cobalt magnets if any stage of production - mining, refining, separation, melting or fabrication - happened in China, Russia, Iran or North Korea. MP is one of only two domestic suppliers positioned to certify compliance, and China's decision on 22 June 2026 to bar dual-use exports to MP only sharpens the case for a domestic chain. If Independence completes qualification with General Motors, Apple shipments start on schedule in 2027, and 10X commissions in 2028, management's medium-term target of $650 million of adjusted profit before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation becomes the base rather than the ceiling, and a 20-times multiple on it - the kind a scarce, government-backed, strategically protected asset can carry - supports the $82 target.
bear_thesis: The bear case is that this was never an event trade, and that what looks like a discount is a story that has simply started to de-rate. Three specific risks carry it. First, the profitability is currently the taxpayer's, not the customers'. Of the $132.9 million headline of 'revenue and price-protection income' in the first quarter of 2026, $42.3 million was the government top-up; strip it out and the quarter's $36.6 million adjusted profit becomes a loss of roughly $6 million. On a trailing twelve-month basis the company earned $19 million of profit before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation on $348 million of revenue and lost $71 million at the bottom line, while free cash flow stayed negative. At $43.13 the enterprise value is about $7.9 billion - roughly 12 times an adjusted profit target that requires a $1.25 billion plant that has not been built. Second, the load-bearing revenue has no date. Magnetics revenue of $21.1 million is precursor material, not finished magnets; the Independence plant is still in product qualification with General Motors; the chief financial officer would not commit to a date for the 1,000-tonne nameplate; Apple shipments begin some time in 2027; 10X commissioning begins some time in 2028. A thesis made of half-year windows slips quietly and repeatedly, and the 1 January 2027 statutory deadline has itself already been postponed once, from 1 January 2026, for exactly the reason that would justify postponing it again - not enough compliant supply. Third, the supply-timing argument may run backwards. The International Energy Agency's 20 July 2026 outlook - rare-earth mining output outside China potentially tripling by 2035 - knocked the whole sector, and the consensus view of a tight 2026-2027 followed by an oxide glut in 2028-2029 puts the price break in the same year 10X starts up. Add China's 22 June 2026 export-control listing, which restricts MP's access to the Chinese equipment, tooling and consumables a magnet line needs, and the execution risk on 10X is higher than the schedule implies. The tape agrees: the stock is down 57% from its 52-week high, printed a new low of $41.12 on 24 July, the chief executive sold roughly $77 million of stock between January and early June at $64-71, and analyst targets have begun to break - the only target published in the last month is $71.50 and Barclays cut to $65 on 16 July. In that world the shares do not stop at $35, because nothing is there: common book equity is about $11 a share and net cash about $3.50.
sop_bull: Event-win value of about $82 a share, which is the fully-built platform discounted back, not a contractual payout. Build: management's medium-term target of $650 million of adjusted profit before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation assumes Mountain Pass at roughly 6,000 tonnes a year of NdPr and the magnet business running across Independence (1,000 tonnes, doubling toward 2,000 with Apple) and 10X (7,000 tonnes). Split roughly $300-350 million to the upstream and midstream materials business and $300-350 million to magnetics, of which $140 million a year is contractually guaranteed by the government for ten years once 10X is built. Put 20 times on that $650 million - the multiple a scarce, protected, government-backed strategic asset can carry when the sourcing mandate has teeth - for an enterprise value of $13.0 billion; add today's $1.74 billion of cash and short-term investments, subtract $1.05 billion of debt and about $0.8 billion of incremental borrowing needed to finish 10X, and divide by roughly 200 million diluted shares: about $67. Layer on the upside case for the commodity - NdPr holding above the $110 floor, where MP keeps 70% of the excess, and a China-driven squeeze into the 1 January 2027 defence certification cliff adding, say, $150 million of incremental profit - and the same 20 times takes it to roughly $82. That reconciles with the street: consensus median target $81, high $100, low $69.
sop_bear: The verified downside is about $32 a share, and it is a reference point rather than a backstop - there is no contract, cash balance or asset that stops the price at the board's $35. Build, from the 31 March 2026 balance sheet: cash and short-term investments of $1.74 billion less total debt of $1.05 billion is $0.69 billion of net cash, about $3.50 a share. Common book equity - total equity of $2.38 billion less the $414 million of preferred stock held by the government - is about $1.97 billion, or roughly $11 a share, and the fixed assets behind it are a mine and half-built plants that no one else can operate at scale. So the true asset floor is $11, not $35. What is defensible above that is the $30.03 a share at which the Department of Defense converts its preferred and strikes its warrant: that is the price the best-informed and most motivated buyer in the story agreed to pay in July 2025, before the ramp de-risked anything, and it is the level at which the government's own economics and the ten-year $110-per-kilogram price floor plus the $140 million annual profit guarantee on 10X (worth roughly $3 a share discounted back) become the dominant support. Round to $32. Reaching it requires only what the bear case describes: a magnet ramp that slips past 2027, the government top-up disappearing as NdPr trades above the floor, and the 2028-2029 oxide glut arriving on schedule.
sop_breakdown: A probability-weighted blend of two outcomes, because no single discounted cash flow is honest for a company whose earnings begin at the end of the decade. Favourable resolution - Independence qualifies with General Motors, Apple shipments start in 2027, 10X commissions in 2028, and the 1 January 2027 defence sourcing mandate pulls domestic magnet demand forward - gets $82, weighted 40%, for $32.80. Adverse resolution - the ramp slips, the government top-up fades as the commodity trades above the floor, and the 2028-2029 oxide glut lands as 10X starts up - gets $32, weighted 60%, for $19.20. Sum: about $52 a share, call it a $48-56 range. Underneath, the parts at scale would be roughly $300-350 million of profit before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation from the materials business (Mountain Pass mining and separation, currently running at a $147 million annual rate but roughly half of that is the government price top-up) and $300-350 million from magnetics (Independence plus 10X, of which $140 million a year is contractually guaranteed), against $0.69 billion of net cash today and $1.25 billion of 10X spending still to come. The 40/60 weighting is deliberately cautious: the favourable branch needs three separate undated ramps to land, while the adverse branch needs only one of them to slip.
risk_reward: About 2.3 to 1 on the honest numbers, not the 4-to-1 the board entry implies. From $43.13: upside to the $82 target is +$38.87, or +90%; downside to the verified $32 reference is -$11.13, or -26%. That is 3.5 to 1 if you accept $32 as a floor - but it is not a contractual floor, and against the real asset backstop of about $11 a share in common book value the ratio collapses to roughly 1.2 to 1. Weighting for the fact that the upside needs three undated ramps and the downside needs one slip, the practical asymmetry is about 2.3 to 1, which is a respectable watchlist number and not a defined-risk special situation. Against the reconciled base case of $52 the upside is +21%.
catalyst_summary: Supply timing, not a dated payout: MP's magnet ramp (Independence still in qualification, Apple shipments 'in 2027', 10X commissioning 'in 2028') sits behind the one hard date that matters, the 1 January 2027 statutory ban on Chinese-origin magnets in US defence systems - a deadline already postponed once from 2026, which pays MP nothing directly, and into which the stock is falling rather than rising, from $43.13 against an $82 street target with no contractual floor beneath it.
dated_milestone: Two dates are real and verified, and neither is a payout. 6 August 2026, after the US close: second-quarter 2026 results and webcast, confirmed by the company on 16 July 2026. This is the first clean read on underlying economics, because NdPr traded above the $110 per kilogram government floor for most of the quarter, so the $42.3 million top-up that carried the first quarter should shrink sharply or vanish - headline profit can fall sequentially even as the business improves. 1 January 2027: the statutory prohibition under the defence acquisition rules implementing Section 844 of the 2021 defence authorisation act takes effect, requiring every US defence contractor to certify that no stage of production of its neodymium-iron-boron or samarium-cobalt magnets occurred in China, Russia, Iran or North Korea. Note the slip: the original effective date was 1 January 2026 and the 2024 defence authorisation act pushed it back a year for lack of compliant supply. Everything else in the story is a window, not a date: heavy rare-earth separation commissioning at Mountain Pass 'imminently', the 1,000-tonne Independence nameplate with no committed date, Apple shipments 'in 2027', 10X commissioning 'beginning in 2028', and the Maaden refinery joint venture in Saudi Arabia still at binding-term-sheet stage with no construction timeline.
forcing_function: The 1 January 2027 defence certification deadline is the only genuine forcing function, and it is an industry event rather than a company event. From that date a US defence contractor cannot use a rare-earth magnet with any Chinese, Russian, Iranian or North Korean step in its production chain without risking contract termination, and MP is one of only two domestic suppliers positioned to certify. What forces a re-rating is not the date itself but the procurement behaviour in front of it: prime contractors qualifying and contracting domestic magnet supply through the second half of 2026. The nearer trigger is the 6 August 2026 second-quarter print, which is where the market finds out whether the magnetics segment is converting precursor sales into qualified finished magnets and what the business earns without the government top-up. A third, slower trigger is the commodity: NdPr recovered from about $90 per kilogram on 1 June to roughly $133 on 1 July 2026, and every dollar above the $110 floor is 70 cents to MP. Against those, note what is absent - there is no merger to close, no regulatory decision on MP itself, no spin, no forced seller clearing, and no activist. This is a production ramp wearing an event's clothes.
consensus_delta: Where we disagree with the market runs in both directions, and that is precisely why we are not paying up. The street is wrong on quality of earnings. The consensus median target of $81 is built on management's $650 million medium-term adjusted profit target and treats the first quarter's $36.6 million as evidence the model works. It is not: $42.3 million of that quarter's headline was the government's price top-up, and without it the quarter was a loss of roughly $6 million. Analysts have also been slow with the pen - the only target published in the last month is $71.50 against a $80.70 quarterly average, and Barclays cut from $69 to $65 on 16 July while keeping a positive rating. Unrevised targets on a stock making 52-week lows are not support; they are unpriced downside, and the August print is where they get marked. The street is also wrong the other way, on the demand cliff. The 1 January 2027 statutory bar on Chinese-origin magnets in US defence systems is barely modelled by anyone as a near-term procurement event, and neither is the second-order effect of China's 22 June 2026 export-control listing, which pushes every American prime contractor to qualify domestic supply faster. Our real edge is on the third question, the one nobody is framing correctly: the market is treating an undated production ramp as though it were a dated event, and pricing MP on 2030 earnings while the 2026 and 2027 cash flows are negative. That is not an expectations arbitrage in our favour - it is the reason to wait.
valley_of_death: The risky window is the next three to nine months and it is unusually well defined. It starts on 6 August 2026. With NdPr trading above the $110 per kilogram floor for most of the second quarter, the government top-up that produced $42.3 million of first-quarter profit should shrink sharply or disappear, so reported adjusted profit can fall sequentially even though the underlying business is better - a print that reads badly for the wrong reason, into a tape that is already selling. Management has also guided to a single-digit sequential decline in NdPr volumes in the second quarter. Second, cash. Free cash flow is negative, 2026 capital spending is guided to $500-600 million, and $1.25 billion of 10X construction is still ahead; cash and short-term investments already fell from $1.83 billion at year-end to $1.74 billion by 31 March. The $1 billion JPMorgan and Goldman Sachs facility and the $150 million government loan cover it, but they convert a net-cash balance sheet into a levered one during the build. Third, procurement risk from China's 22 June 2026 export-control listing: magnet production lines depend on Chinese-origin equipment, tooling and consumables, and MP has not addressed on the record how 10X gets built without them. Fourth, the narrative risk of the 20 July 2026 International Energy Agency outlook and the widely-held view that oxide supply outruns qualified magnet capacity in 2028-2029 - the year 10X commissions. And fifth, the qualification risk itself: if General Motors qualification is not completed and announced before year-end, the 1 January 2027 deadline arrives with MP unable to convert it, which would be the single most damaging outcome available in this window.
positioning_washout: The shareholder base has been through most of a forced-selling cycle but has not capitulated. This is a heavily retail-owned, thematically-held stock: it sits in rare-earth and critical-minerals exchange-traded funds, and it absorbed a wave of momentum and defence-thematic money after the July 2025 government partnership took it from roughly $30 to a $100.25 high. Every one of those buyers is now under water, and the unwind has been orderly rather than climactic - down 13.4% in June on China's export-control listing, down 26.9% over the past month, a 7.5% drop on 24 July on volume only 14% above average to a new low of $41.12, then a 4.4% bounce to $43.13. Volume 14% above average is not a wash-out; a genuine capitulation in a name this widely held looks like three to five times average volume. Two other mechanical flows matter. The company carries convertible notes, so a convertible-arbitrage base is short stock against them and adds supply on rallies. And insider supply has been real and heavy: the chief executive sold roughly 1.2 million shares for about $77 million between January and early June at $64-71, with the verified late-May and early-June tranches printing between $65.20 and $71.31; the one offsetting purchase on the record is the chief operating officer's 10,000 shares at $54.30 on 9 June, now 21% under water. The analyst community has not yet cut, so the marginal seller who reacts to downgrades has not arrived. That seller is the wash-out we are waiting for, and the 6 August print is the most likely trigger for it.
moderator_conclusion: This does not belong in the dated-event book, and calling it one is the mistake to correct first. There is no deal to close, no regulatory decision on MP itself, no spin, no forced seller clearing, no activist. What exists is a genuine strategic asset in the middle of a multi-year construction programme, with two real contractual supports from the US government and one real statutory deadline that helps the whole domestic magnet industry rather than paying MP a defined sum. The supply-timing catalyst on our board is soft and undated, and the events that actually resolve value - Apple shipments in 2027, 10X commissioning in 2028, the $650 million profit target around 2029 - all sit outside any window we can underwrite. Note too that the big event here already fired: the July 2025 government partnership took the stock from about $30 to $100, and the entire re-rate has since round-tripped. The floor is the other half of the problem. The board's $35 has nothing beneath it - common book equity is about $11 a share and net cash about $3.50 - and the only defensible reference below the market is the $30.03 at which the government converts its preferred and strikes its warrant. A stock that has just printed a 52-week low 5% above its claimed floor does not have a floor; it has a chart level. So the asymmetry is not the 4-to-1 the entry implied. It is closer to 2.3-to-1 after weighting, and the reconciled base case of about $52 is only 21% above the market. That is a watchlist, not a purchase. What would change it, specifically: first, a print on 6 August 2026 that shows the magnetics segment converting precursor sales into qualified finished magnets and shows the business roughly breaking even at the profit line without the government top-up; second, a completed General Motors qualification announced before year-end, which is what converts the 1 January 2027 defence certification cliff from an industry headline into MP revenue; or third, a price in the low $30s, near the government's own $30.03 basis, where the most informed buyer in the story would be paying today's price and the margin of safety is real rather than assumed. Until one of those arrives, we watch. The business is strengthening; the entry is not.
interrogator_dossier:
# MP Materials (NYSE: MP) - Forensic Dossier on the Event

### Event-driven review, refreshed 28 July 2026. Live price $43.13 (last quote 27 July 2026, up 4.4% off the prior close of $41.30). The stock printed a fresh 52-week low of $41.12 on 24 July; the 52-week high is $100.25.

**The short version.** This name arrived on our board as an event-driven special situation: a supply-timing catalyst said to close the gap between a mid-$40s share price and an $82 target, with a $35 downside floor. After verifying the facts, that label does not survive contact with the evidence. There is no dated, binding event that pays MP Materials a defined sum. There is a real government partnership, a real production ramp, and one genuine statutory deadline that helps the whole American magnet industry - but the company's own milestone is a half-year window, not a date, and the $35 floor is not backed by any asset, cash balance, or contract. Meanwhile the stock has fallen 57% from its 52-week high, and the chief executive sold roughly $77 million of stock between January and early June at prices between about $64 and $71.

---

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

MP Materials owns Mountain Pass in California, the only large-scale rare-earth mine and separation complex in the United States. The story has moved through three chapters in two years.

Chapter one was the miner: dig ore, sell concentrate, most of it to China. Chapter two, from July 2025, was the transformation. The Department of Defense (now styled the Department of War) took a $400 million convertible preferred stake plus a warrant, together representing 15% of the company on an as-converted basis, at a conversion and exercise price of $30.03 per share. Alongside it came a ten-year commitment that the government will top up MP's realized price for its neodymium-praseodymium ("NdPr" - the magnetic rare-earth pair that actually matters) to a floor of $110 per kilogram, a $150 million loan for heavy rare-earth separation, and a $1 billion financing package from JPMorgan and Goldman Sachs to build a magnet plant called 10X, with the government committing to buy 100% of 10X output for ten years after construction and guaranteeing $140 million a year of profit before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation from it.

Chapter three is the one being underwritten now: turning that paper into magnets. The company stopped selling concentrate to China entirely (concentrate revenue went from $30.1 million in the first quarter of 2025 to zero in the first quarter of 2026), made its first commercial neodymium-iron-boron magnets at its Independence facility in Fort Worth in December 2025, selected a 120-acre site in Northlake, Texas for 10X in February 2026, and broke ground there during the first quarter. 10X is a $1.25 billion, 7,000-tonne-a-year project that would take total US magnet capacity to 10,000 tonnes; commissioning is scheduled to begin in 2028.

The quiet narrative shift worth noticing: management now emphasises the scarcity of NdPr as the binding constraint for the next several years rather than emphasising near-term magnet delivery. That is a subtle move from a schedule you can be held to toward a market condition you cannot.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Management claim | The evidence | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| "Record NdPr production and sales with solid adjusted EBITDA" (first quarter 2026) | Revenue $90.6 million, up 49% year over year; NdPr production 917 tonnes, up 63%; NdPr sales 1,006 tonnes, up 117%; total rare-earth oxide production 12,983 tonnes, up 6%; adjusted profit before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation of $36.6 million against a $2.7 million loss a year earlier | Holds up. The mine and separation plant are genuinely working. |
| The business is turning profitable | Adjusted diluted earnings of $0.03 per share, but reported diluted earnings were still a loss of $0.04, and $42.3 million of the $132.9 million "revenue and price-protection income" headline came from the government top-up rather than from customers. Strip that payment out and the quarter's adjusted profit of $36.6 million becomes a loss of roughly $6 million | Poorer than the headline. The reported profitability is, on these figures, funded by the taxpayer. |
| "$1.7 billion of cash and short-term investments fully funds our long-term capital plan" | Cash and short-term investments fell from $1.83 billion at end-2025 to $1.74 billion at 31 March 2026, against $1.05 billion of total debt (net cash of roughly $0.7 billion), with 2026 capital spending guided to $500-600 million and $1.25 billion of 10X spending still ahead | Directionally true today, tight by 2028. Free cash flow is still negative and the cushion is being spent. |
| Independence is transitioning to finished magnets | Magnetics revenue was $21.1 million, up 306%, but it is precursor material, not finished magnets. The facility remains in product qualification with its foundational customer, General Motors, and the chief financial officer declined to commit to a date for reaching the 1,000-tonne nameplate. Shipments to Apple, under a $500 million partnership, are scheduled to begin in 2027 | This is the crux. The revenue that carries the thesis has not started. |

Valuation reality check, because the special-situation framing depends on the price being low. At $43.13 the equity is worth about $8.6 billion on the fully diluted share count of roughly 199 million, and with $1.74 billion of cash and short-term investments against $1.05 billion of debt the enterprise value (equity plus debt, less cash) is roughly $7.9 billion. Trailing twelve-month revenue is $348 million, trailing profit before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation is $19 million, and the trailing bottom line is a loss of $71 million. Against management's own medium-term target of $650 million of adjusted profit before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation - a figure that requires 10X to be built and running - the shares trade at about 12 times. That is not a cheap-and-bad asset waiting for an event. It is a strategically important asset priced on earnings that arrive at the end of the decade.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY - Rising, and worth discounting for it

The founder and chief executive James Litinsky called 2026 a consequential year and said the company had broken ground on 10X and was advancing every aspect of the project with urgency. Confidence is high and the operating results support most of it. What has not risen alongside the confidence is specificity: the magnet-delivery language has drifted from a commitment toward a hedge, promising initial magnet revenue in 2026 beginning with modest deliveries as capacity ramps over the following several quarters.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY - Medium

Production guidance has been met and beaten. The company said it would raise NdPr output and it did, by 63% year over year, and it holds to a 500-tonne-per-month exit rate for 2026 while warning of a single-digit sequential decline in the second quarter. That is the behaviour of a management team that forecasts what it controls.

Downstream guidance is where credibility thins. The 1,000-tonne magnet nameplate has no committed date, customer qualification with General Motors is unfinished, and the operating-cost promise - bringing cash costs from over $60 per kilogram down to $40 - was defended with the caveat that a snapshot in time obscures the underlying figure. Cost targets defended by explaining why the number you can see is not the real number deserve a discount.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

Three questions recur and none gets a clean answer. When will Independence reach nameplate? Deflected into qualification complexity. What comes after General Motors, Apple and the government? Deferred to future announcements. How should the magnetics segment be modelled quarter to quarter? Acknowledged as lumpy, then set aside.

There is a fourth question analysts are not asking loudly enough. On 22 June 2026 China's Ministry of Commerce placed MP Materials on its export-control list, barring Chinese firms from exporting dual-use goods to it and barring anyone anywhere from transferring Chinese-origin dual-use products to it. The company sells nothing to China, so the sales exposure is nil - but a magnet plant needs Chinese-origin equipment, tooling and consumables, and the squeeze lands on procurement for 10X, exactly the project the valuation rests on. The stock fell 13.4% in June on the news. Management has not addressed the procurement question on the record.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

Concerning:
- Insider selling into strength on a large scale. The chief executive sold roughly 1.2 million shares for about $77 million between January and early June 2026; the verified late-May and early-June sales alone ran from $65.20 to $71.31 a share. The stock now trades at $43.13. The one offsetting purchase on the record is the chief operating officer buying 10,000 shares at $54.30 on 9 June 2026 - which is itself now 21% under water.
- The load-bearing revenue has no date. First finished-magnet revenue is a half-year window, and the customer qualification behind it is incomplete.
- A structural counter-argument has appeared. On 20 July 2026 the International Energy Agency's outlook - that rare-earth mining output outside China could triple by 2035 - sent the whole sector lower on oversupply fears. Sector commentary now points to a tight market through 2026-2027 followed by a possible NdPr price break in 2028-2029, as oxide supply from MP, Lynas, Arafura and Pensana outruns qualified magnet capacity. That would arrive exactly as 10X commissions.
- Free cash flow is still negative with $500-600 million of annual capital spending ahead and a cash balance already declining. Share count has grown too: the weighted diluted count rose from 163.8 million in mid-2025 to 177.7 million basic and 199.2 million diluted by the first quarter of 2026.
- Wall Street targets are beginning to break. The consensus median is still about $81, but the single target published in the last month sits at $71.50, and Barclays cut its target from $69 to $65 on 16 July while keeping a positive rating. Unrevised targets are not support; they are unpriced downside.

Encouraging:
- The government price floor is real and contractual: $110 per kilogram of NdPr for ten years from the fourth quarter of 2025, with the state covering any shortfall and taking 30% of the excess when the market pays more. A contractual floor under cash flow is genuinely rare in a commodity business.
- The commodity is currently well above that floor. The NdPr benchmark bottomed near $90 per kilogram on 1 June 2026 and recovered to roughly $133 by 1 July, so the company is earning the market price and needs no subsidy today.
- Operating execution is real: record volumes, positive adjusted profit before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation, the first positive gross profit since 2024, groundbreaking on schedule, and a clean exit from Chinese concentrate sales.
- A hard, statutory demand cliff exists. Under the defence acquisition rules implementing Section 844 of the 2021 defence authorisation act, from 1 January 2027 no US defence contractor may use neodymium-iron-boron or samarium-cobalt magnets if any stage of production - mining, refining, separation, melting or fabrication - occurred in China, Russia, Iran or North Korea. Failure to certify risks contract termination, and MP is one of only two domestic suppliers positioned to certify.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

The government's entry price is the most informative number nobody quotes. The Department of Defense converts at $30.03 per share and its warrant strikes at $30.03. That is the price at which the most informed and most motivated buyer in this story agreed to own it, one year ago, before the ramp de-risked anything. The share price is now $43.13 - still 44% above the state's basis, not below it.

Second signal: management's own framing has migrated from delivery to scarcity. When a company stops promising a shipment date and starts describing a multi-year supply shortage, the investable claim has moved from something verifiable to something unfalsifiable.

Third: the statutory magnet ban has already slipped once. The original effective date was 1 January 2026; the 2024 defence authorisation act pushed it to 1 January 2027 to give contractors time to find alternative suppliers. A deadline that has been extended once for exactly the reason that would apply again - insufficient compliant supply - is not a deadline you should size a position against.

Fourth, and this one is dated: the second-quarter results land after the close on Thursday 6 August 2026. With NdPr trading above the $110 floor for most of the quarter, the government top-up that produced $42.3 million of the first quarter's profit should shrink sharply or disappear. That makes the August print the first clean read on what this business earns on its own - and it means headline profit can fall sequentially even as the underlying business improves.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

Trajectory: strengthening. The mine, the separation plant and the balance sheet are all in better shape than a year ago, and the government partnership is a genuine competitive asset, not a press release.

But the single thing the director must weigh is this: **the event this position was supposed to trade is not an event.** There is no deal to close, no regulatory decision on MP itself, no spin, no forced seller clearing. The catalyst is a production ramp whose date the company will not give, standing in front of an industry deadline that has already been postponed once and that pays MP nothing directly. And the claimed $35 downside floor has nothing underneath it: common book equity is about $11 per share, net cash is about $3.50 per share, and the only defensible reference point below the market is the government's own $30.03 basis. The stock is making new lows with no asset backstop within 60% of the price.

On the moat: narrow but real, and of the regulatory-and-scarce-asset type rather than the brand or switching-cost type. Mountain Pass cannot be replicated quickly, and the ten-year price floor plus guaranteed offtake are contractual advantages competitors do not have. The trend is stable - 10X and the 2027 sourcing mandate would widen it, the tripling of non-Chinese supply by 2035 and the arrival of rivals such as Energy Fuels, USA Rare Earth and Noveon would narrow it, and those roughly cancel over a five-year view. The secular threat to terminal value is manageable rather than material: rare-earth magnets are structurally in demand and the American sourcing mandate is a durable tailwind. What is at risk is not the business's existence but the scarcity premium in its multiple, which is a valuation problem, not a terminal one.
